facts.value: For one query row, each score q_i is paired with a value vector v_i of width 128 for i in [0, 4096).
The output is o = (sum_i exp(q_i - M) * v_i) / D, where M = max_i(q_i) and D = sum_i exp(q_i - M).
The implementation first finds M, then writes per-element exp(q_i - M), then reduces D, then writes weighted vectors, then reduces the weighted vectors, then divides.
There are 4096 elements per row, value width is 128, and a batch contains 2048 independent rows.
Inputs and outputs use FP16; accumulation may use FP32. Forward max_abs_error <= 3e-4 and backward relative error <= 2e-3 against the reference.
A causal mask may remove a suffix of each row; the valid prefix length can differ by row.
A full per-row weighted-vector intermediate would exceed the intended on-chip budget. A 64-element key/value tile and two row-width scratch buffers are available.
The target GPU has 128 registers per thread as the practical occupancy budget; the current implementation uses 96 registers per thread.
